name: Mississippi

excluded: Farm laborers (unless employer has 5+ regular non-farm employees)
Corporate officers (up to 4 may elect out)

benefitCategories.medical: All reasonable and necessary treatment; no physician choice limitation initially
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max ($596.06/week 2024—lowest in nation); max 450 weeks
benefitCategories.temporaryPartial: 66 2/3% of wage difference up to max
benefitCategories.permanentPartial: Schedule for specific loss (weeks × 66 2/3%); non-schedule by loss of wage-earning capacity
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max; 450 weeks (then may petition for additional if still totally disabled)
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 66 2/3% of wages to dependents; max 450 weeks; $5,000 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: First Report of Injury (Form B-3) by employer; Petition to Controvert (B-5/B-5-11) to dispute

appealLevels.name: Administrative Law Judge (ALJ)
appealLevels.deadline: 2 years from injury or last payment

workersCompensation.penalties: Penalties for uninsured employers; interest on late payments; additional compensation for unreasonable delay

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Mississippi has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: Mississippi Medicaid
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Mississippi has not expanded Medicaid under ACA

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families
programs.eligibility: Very low income families with children; very strict limits

statutes.name: No Comprehensive State Civil Rights Law
statutes.note: Mississippi has NO state law prohibiting private employment discrimination based on race, sex, religion, or disability—one of two states (with Alabama) without such a law

protectedClasses: No state-protected classes for private employment discrimination
civilRightsFramework.federalReliance: CRITICAL: Mississippi workers must rely ENTIRELY on federal law (Title VII, ADA, ADEA, Section 1981) for employment discrimination protection. No state remedy exists.
civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Only federal anti-retaliation provisions apply to private employers

accommodationObligations.standard: Federal ADA applies to employers with 15+ employees only
accommodationObligations.gap: Employees at small employers (<15) have NO disability accommodation rights

enablingStatutes.civilRights: NO STATE CIVIL RIGHTS EMPLOYMENT LAW

delegatedBodies.note: No state civil rights agency for employment; EEOC only venue

laborStandards.authority: Federal DOL/WHD handles FLSA; Mississippi has no state minimum wage above federal ($7.25)

civilRights.authority: No state enforcement; EEOC handles all employment discrimination

occupationalSafety.authority: Mississippi is not a state plan state; OSHA covers private sector

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 2 years from injury or last voluntary payment
filingDeadlines.eeocCharge: 180 days from discriminatory act (no state agency worksharing)

judicialReview.wc: ALJ → Full Commission → Circuit Court → Supreme Court
judicialReview.note: No state court remedy for employment discrimination

specialConsiderations.lowestBenefits: Mississippi has the LOWEST maximum weekly WC benefit in the entire United States at $596.06/week (2024); severely inadequate for any worker earning above poverty wages
specialConsiderations.noCivilRightsLaw: Mississippi is one of only TWO states (with Alabama) that has NO state law prohibiting employment discrimination in the private sector. All claims must go through federal EEOC/courts.
specialConsiderations.shortEeocDeadline: Because there is no state agency, the EEOC deadline is only 180 days—significantly shorter than in states with worksharing agreements (300 days)
specialConsiderations.limitedProtections: Workers at small employers (<5 for WC, <15 for ADA) have essentially no workplace injury or discrimination protections beyond common law
specialConsiderations.healthcareAccess: With Medicaid not expanded and low WC benefits, injured workers face significant healthcare access barriers
